Q35484: The second holiest city in Islam, in the Hejaz region of Saudi Arabia.
The Prophet Muhammad moved here from Mecca in 622 (the Hijra, start of the Islamic calendar) and is buried here.
The Prophet's Mosque (Al-Masjid an-Nabawi) is one of the largest mosques in the world.
Q1519: Capital of the United Arab Emirates, on a T-shaped island in the Persian Gulf.
The richest emirate, holding most of the UAE's oil; its sovereign wealth fund is among the largest in the world.
Landmarks: the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque and the Louvre Abu Dhabi.
Hosts the Abu Dhabi Formula 1 Grand Prix on Yas Island.
Q198266: City in Hunan on the Xiang River, part of the Changsha–Zhuzhou–Xiangtan cluster.
One of China's biggest railway hubs and makers of electric locomotives (CRRC Zhuzhou).
Grew from a small town into an industrial city in the 1950s.
Liling, in the prefecture, is famous for porcelain and fireworks.
Q3110: Capital of El Salvador, in a valley below the San Salvador volcano.
Founded by the Spanish in 1525; has been damaged by many earthquakes.
Archbishop Óscar Romero, now a saint, was murdered here in 1980.
Its metro area holds over a third of the country's people.
Q3688: Capital of Mauritania, on the Atlantic edge of the Sahara.
Built from scratch from 1958 as a capital for the new country; planned for only 15,000 people.
Grew rapidly as droughts in the 1970s drove nomads and farmers to the city.
Sand dunes reach into the city; its fish market is famous.
Q404763: The largest prefecture by area in Henan, in the southwest.
Home region of famous historical figures: the astronomer Zhang Heng, the physician Zhang Zhongjing and strategist Zhuge Liang.
Known for jade carving (Dushan jade) and as the start of the South–North Water Transfer central route at Danjiangkou.
Q574593: Oil city in Delta State in the Niger Delta.
A major port and refinery city, and capital of the colonial Warri Province.
Home of the Itsekiri kingdom, as well as Urhobo and Ijaw peoples.
Known in Nigeria for its witty 'Warri' humour and comedians.
Q2733647: Small town (Nagar Panchayat) in Siwan district, Bihar.
Part of the densely populated Bhojpuri-speaking region of western Bihar.
Q330531: Third city of Rajasthan, on the Chambal River.
Famous as India's coaching capital: hundreds of thousands of students prepare there for engineering and medical exams.
Capital of the Kota princely state; known for Kota miniature paintings and Kota Doria saris.
Claims to be India's first traffic-light-free city.
Q58650: City in northwestern Hebei, on the old route between Beijing and Mongolia; known as Kalgan.
Called the 'Northern Gate of Beijing' and a strategic Great Wall pass (Dajingmen).
Its Chongli district co-hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics skiing events.
A big wind and solar power area.
Q425492: City in Sichuan at the confluence of the Tuo and Yangtze rivers.
Called the 'Liquor City': home of Luzhou Laojiao, one of China's oldest baijiu makers (cellars from 1573).
Q496405: City in eastern Yunnan, called the 'throat of Yunnan' on the route to Guizhou.
The Pearl River has its source in the prefecture.
Known for tobacco and coal; the Luoping rapeseed flower fields are famous.
Q185518: Myanmar's second city, on the Irrawaddy River.
Founded in 1857 by King Mindon; the last royal capital of Burma before British annexation in 1885.
The centre of Burmese culture and Buddhism, with Mandalay Hill and many monasteries.
Nearby are the old capitals Amarapura (with the U Bein teak bridge), Inwa and Mingun.
Q168652: Capital of the self-declared Republic of Somaliland, which is internationally considered part of Somalia.
Grew as a watering and trading stop of the Isaaq clans.
Almost destroyed by Siad Barre's air force in 1988 during the civil war.
Near the Laas Geel caves with some of Africa's oldest rock paintings.
Q2096: Capital of Alberta, on the North Saskatchewan River; the northernmost North American city with over a million people.
Began as a Hudson's Bay Company fur-trading fort in 1795.
Gateway to Alberta's oil sands and the north; called the 'Festival City'.
West Edmonton Mall was the world's largest mall in the 1980s.
Q466216: City in the Yemeni highlands near the Red Sea port of Mocha, at about 1,400 m.
Was the capital of Yemen under Imam Ahmad (1948–1962).
Has long been considered Yemen's cultural capital.
Divided and besieged during the Yemeni civil war.
Q20921: South Korea's fifth-largest city, in the centre of the country.
A science city: home of KAIST and the Daedeok Innopolis research district.
Grew as a railway town; hosted the Expo 1993.
Next to the new administrative city of Sejong.
Q132754: Capital of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq; Kurds call it Hewlêr.
One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities, around a 6,000-year-old citadel mound.
The Citadel of Erbil is a World Heritage Site.
Near the site of the Battle of Gaugamela (331 BC) where Alexander defeated Darius III.
Q200878: City in Madhya Pradesh on the Narmada River.
Snooker is said to have been invented by British officers here in 1875.
Famous for the Marble Rocks gorge at Bhedaghat.
A big army cantonment and seat of the state High Court.
Q7258412: Puebla, capital of the Mexican state of the same name, was founded by the Spanish in 1531 between Mexico City and Veracruz.
Its historic centre with colourful Talavera-tiled buildings is a World Heritage Site.
Origin of mole poblano sauce and chiles en nogada.
The Battle of Puebla (5 May 1862) against the French is the origin of Cinco de Mayo; the Great Pyramid of Cholula is nearby.
Q131620: Capital of Rio Grande do Norte, near Brazil's northeastern tip.
Founded on Christmas Day 1599, hence the name ('Natal' = Christmas).
Known for its huge sand dunes and the Forte dos Reis Magos.
Was a key Allied air base in WWII, the 'Trampoline to Victory' to Africa.
Q1999000: Capital of Akwa Ibom State in southeastern Nigeria, created in 1987.
Known for its Godswill Akpabio stadium and as headquarters of Ibom Air.
Q10395: Port city on the north coast of Java, on the border of West and Central Java.
A historic sultanate; its Kasepuhan and Kanoman palaces mix Javanese, Chinese and European styles.
One of the Wali Songo, Sunan Gunung Jati, spread Islam from here.
Known for its colourful batik with cloud ('mega mendung') patterns.
Q360178: City in Anhui on the Huai River.
Known for coal mining and power plants.
Considered the birthplace of tofu, said to have been invented by Liu An, the Han-dynasty Prince of Huainan.
Liu An's court wrote the 'Huainanzi', a classic of Chinese thought.
Q1011138: County-level city in Zhejiang under Jinhua.
Home of the Yiwu International Trade City, the world's largest wholesale market for small goods.
Most of the world's Christmas decorations are traded here.
Linked by freight train to Madrid, one of the world's longest railway routes.
Q131301: City on the Orontes River in western Syria, called Emesa in antiquity.
Home city of the Roman emperor Elagabalus and the Severan dynasty empresses.
The Krak des Chevaliers Crusader castle is nearby.
Heavily destroyed during the Syrian civil war ('capital of the revolution').
Q3674: Capital of Niger, on the Niger River.
Grew from small villages after the French chose it as the colonial capital in 1926.
Known for its Grand Mosque and the Niger National Museum.
One of the hottest capitals in the world.
Q43070: Industrial city in eastern Ukraine, the main city of the Donbas coal region.
Founded in 1869 by the Welsh businessman John Hughes as Yuzovka (Hughesovka); later called Stalino.
Called the 'city of a million roses'; home of FC Shakhtar Donetsk.
Q42664: City in northern Zhejiang on the south shore of Lake Tai.
Famous for Huzhou writing brushes, one of the 'Four Treasures of the Study'.
Nanxun is one of the classic water towns; Anji county is known for bamboo and white tea.
Q158467: City in Madhya Pradesh dominated by Gwalior Fort on a hilltop.
A temple inside the fort has the oldest known inscription of the number zero as a numeral (9th century).
Home of the Scindia dynasty; known as a centre of Hindustani classical music (Tansen's tomb).
The Jai Vilas Palace has huge chandeliers.
Q225641: Kenya's second city and main port, on an island off the Indian Ocean coast.
An old Swahili trading town since about 900 AD; contested by Portuguese, Omani Arabs and the British.
Fort Jesus, built by the Portuguese in 1593, is a World Heritage Site.
Start of the railway to Uganda and of the new Mombasa–Nairobi standard-gauge line.
Q59164: City in Guangdong on the Xi River west of Guangzhou.
The Jesuit Matteo Ricci lived here from 1583, starting the Christian mission to China.
Famous for Duan inkstones, among the finest in China.
Known for the Seven Star Crags and Dinghu Mountain.
Q28441: Capital of Maranhão, on an island in the Atlantic.
The only Brazilian state capital founded by the French (1612), later taken by the Portuguese.
Its historic centre with tile-covered colonial houses is a World Heritage Site.
Known as Brazil's 'reggae capital' and for the Bumba Meu Boi festival.
Q146723: Capital of Tshopo province in DR Congo, on the Congo River near Boyoma Falls.
Formerly Stanleyville, named after the explorer Henry Morton Stanley.
The furthest point upriver navigable from Kinshasa; Joseph Conrad's 'Heart of Darkness' was inspired by a trip here.
Was a centre of Patrice Lumumba's movement.
Q404817: City in eastern Henan, an early centre of the Shang dynasty.
Considered the origin of Chinese merchants: 'shang' means both the Shang people and 'trade'.
Its ancient Guide (Gui De) city wall and moat are well preserved.
Q580876: Fast-growing twin city in the Mumbai metropolitan region, in Palghar district.
Mainly a commuter city on Mumbai's Western Railway line.
Q3882: Capital of Bahrain, an island kingdom in the Persian Gulf.
An old pearling and trading port; ruled by Portuguese, Persians and later under British protection until 1971.
The Qal'at al-Bahrain fort is a World Heritage Site of the ancient Dilmun civilisation.
Linked to Saudi Arabia by the King Fahd Causeway; hosts the Bahrain Formula 1 Grand Prix.
Q4803: City in Central Java, commonly called Solo.
Seat of two royal courts: the Kasunanan palace and the Mangkunegaran palace.
A centre of Javanese culture and batik.
Hometown of President Joko Widodo, who was its mayor.
Q360769: China's biggest market for traditional Chinese medicine herbs.
Hometown of Cao Cao, the Three Kingdoms warlord, and of the physician Hua Tuo.
Q887: Russia's fourth-largest city, in the Urals at the border of Europe and Asia.
Founded in 1723 and named after Empress Catherine I; called Sverdlovsk in Soviet times (1924–1991).
The last Tsar Nicholas II and his family were executed here in 1918.
Birthplace of Boris Yeltsin; a big industrial centre.
Q41283: City in southwestern South Korea, merged with South Jeolla Province in 2026.
The 1980 Gwangju Uprising for democracy was violently crushed by the military; the 18 May memorial honours it.
Known for its art Biennale and Korean food.
Q48320: Port city in Hyōgo Prefecture on Osaka Bay, backed by the Rokko mountains.
One of the first ports opened to foreign trade (1868); its Kitano district has old Western houses.
Devastated by the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake, which killed over 6,000 people.
Gave its name to Kobe beef.
Q16557: The third-largest city in Texas, core of the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex.
President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dealey Plaza in 1963.
Grew with cotton, oil and banking; home of the Dallas Cowboys.
Has the largest arts district in the US.
Q5584396: City in eastern Uttar Pradesh on the Rapti River.
Named after the yogi Gorakhnath; the Gorakhnath Math is the seat of a major Hindu order.
Gita Press here is the world's largest publisher of Hindu religious texts.
Its railway station has one of the world's longest platforms (about 1.4 km).
Q58178: City in northern Zhejiang on the Grand Canal, between Shanghai and Hangzhou.
The Chinese Communist Party's first congress finished on a boat on South Lake here in 1921.
Wuzhen and Xitang water towns are in the prefecture.
Q48403: City in Indian Punjab near the Pakistani border; the holiest city of Sikhism.
The Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) is the most important Sikh shrine.
Site of the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre by British troops.
The Wagah–Attari border ceremony with Pakistan is held daily nearby.
Q208471: City in Henan on the south bank of the Yellow River; one of China's Eight Ancient Capitals.
As Bianjing it was the capital of the Northern Song dynasty, then one of the largest cities in the world.
The famous scroll 'Along the River During the Qingming Festival' shows its life.
Had a historic Jewish community for centuries.
Q57931: City in central Jiangsu on the north bank of the Yangtze.
Hometown of Mei Lanfang, the most famous Peking opera performer.
A centre of shipbuilding and the pharmaceutical industry.
Q49259: The most populous city in Virginia, on the Atlantic at the mouth of Chesapeake Bay.
Cape Henry was the first landing place of the English colonists of Jamestown in 1607.
A resort city with a long beach boardwalk.
Part of the Hampton Roads area with the world's largest naval base at Norfolk.
Q17042: City in the East Bay across from San Francisco.
Its port is one of the busiest container ports in the US.
Birthplace of the Black Panther Party (1966).
Known for its diverse population and Lake Merritt.
Q373023: Port city at the eastern tip of Shandong; the closest mainland Chinese city to South Korea.
Was the British leased territory Weihaiwei from 1898 to 1930.
The Qing Beiyang Fleet was destroyed at Liugong Island in the 1895 Sino-Japanese War.
Known as a clean coastal city and for sea cucumbers.
Q404873: The southernmost city of Henan, near Hubei and Anhui.
Famous for Xinyang Maojian, one of China's top green teas.
Jigong Mountain, a summer resort with old villas, is nearby.
Q138589: Provincial capital on Thailand's eastern seaboard, about 100 km southeast of Bangkok.
Forms a metro area with Si Racha and Pattaya.
Famous for its yearly buffalo racing festival.
Part of the Eastern Economic Corridor with the Laem Chabang port.
Q426644: City in central Sichuan on the Fu River.
Considered the hometown of Guanyin, the Buddhist goddess of mercy, in Chinese tradition.
The Chinese Dead Sea salt lake resort is in Daying county.
Q330643: City in Uttar Pradesh on the Ramganga River.
Called 'Pital Nagri' (Brass City) for its brass handicrafts exported worldwide.
Founded in 1600 and named after Mughal prince Murad Bakhsh.
Q147402: The most populous municipality of Jalisco, part of the Guadalajara metro area.
Its Basilica holds the 16th-century Virgin of Zapopan; every October a huge procession brings her back.
Home of the Estadio Akron of Chivas Guadalajara.
The name means 'among the sapote trees'.
Q1025444: County-level city under Changsha, the easternmost part of Hunan.
The 'Fireworks Capital of the World': fireworks have been made here for over 1,000 years.
Hometown of Tan Sitong, a reformer of the 1898 Hundred Days' Reform.
Q164234: City in Kanagawa between Tokyo and Yokohama.
The only Japanese city with over a million people that is not a prefectural capital.
Part of the Keihin industrial zone; home of Fujitsu and Toshiba plants.
Known for the Fujiko F. Fujio (Doraemon) Museum and the Kanamara Matsuri festival.
Q37836: The largest city in Wisconsin, on Lake Michigan.
Famous for beer brewing (Miller, Pabst, Schlitz), brought by German immigrants.
Home of Harley-Davidson motorcycles and its museum.
Hosts Summerfest, one of the largest music festivals in the world.
Q1930: Capital of Canada, on the Ottawa River across from Gatineau, Quebec.
Chosen as capital by Queen Victoria in 1857 as a compromise between English and French Canada.
The Rideau Canal (World Heritage Site) becomes a 7.8 km skating rink in winter.
Parliament Hill is the seat of government.
